notScoredReason: Genuine-business anchors reference verdicts recorded under the v1 criteria. Re-scoring them here would mix a fresh Critic's numbers with old ones inside one stratum mean.

criterionScores.note: There is no visible visual thesis beyond a restrained white page, dark text and one green button; the treatment feels assembled from defaults.
The service list and Bristol references are specific in copy, but the design itself could be reused almost unchanged by any local trade business.

Services, coverage and contact details appear in a sensible one-page order, but the architecture is extremely shallow and provides no visible routes to service detail, credentials, proof or project examples.

The proposition, supporting copy and phone CTA establish a clear first read, followed by plainly differentiated sections. Beyond that opening hierarchy, each section receives nearly identical treatment and weight.
Type is readable and consistent with reasonable measures and line spacing, but appears largely default and does no meaningful compositional or brand work.

The desktop layout is orderly, but the page is a succession of similarly spaced text blocks separated by rules. Mobile spacing is tidy yet somewhat inflated, producing a long scroll without meaningful changes in density or emphasis.

The page relies entirely on ordinary typography, rules and a button. No photography, certification treatment, project evidence, service imagery or distinctive graphic system helps demonstrate the work or establish trust.
A prominent phone button and simple navigation are visible, but screenshots provide no evidence of hover, focus, transition or feedback states; the static controls show only baseline styling.
The mobile view remains readable and the two service columns stack cleanly, but it is essentially the desktop composition collapsed into one column rather than a phone-specific redesign.
The plain, direct presentation is plausible for a local plumbing firm, but almost nothing visually identifies Ardley or conveys workmanship, reliability, locality or heating expertise.

The business, location, principal services, coverage and phone action are immediately understandable. It falls short of stronger commercial work because the page offers little reassurance beyond a registration number and makes no visible case through reviews, guarantees, experience or completed work.

It avoids most conspicuous generated-design motifs such as glowing gradients, card grids, fake metrics and decorative blobs. Its weakness is generic austerity rather than fashionable AI ornament, and the choices still do not feel traceable to this particular business.
There is no distinctive visual, composition, interaction or content device likely to remain identifiable after viewing comparable local-service websites.

verdicts.rationale: The page is clear, readable and functional, but it looks like minimally styled boilerplate rather than authored professional work. It communicates the core service and phone action effectively, yet lacks trust-building evidence, business-specific visual material, responsive invention and any memorable brand expression.

criterionScores.note: The warm neutral palette and mixed serif, sans and monospaced type suggest a rustic bakery direction, but the inconsistent borders, fills, corner radii and controls prevent it becoming a coherent visual thesis.

Bread varieties, fermentation details, collection timing and the physical address are specific, but the design structure itself is a generic product-card landing page that could accommodate many small retailers.

For this small offering, the sequence from proposition to weekly products, collection and location is concise and sensible. The screenshots provide no evidence about deeper routes or whether ordering details are organized effectively beyond this page.

The business name, weekly range and ordering CTA are easy to find, but the three product cards receive inconsistent visual emphasis for no evident reason, and the lower sections flatten into similarly weighted boxes.

Text is legible, but the serif section headings, sans-serif display name and widely tracked monospaced labels do not feel fully reconciled. The mobile product text also has awkward measures and line breaks, while button typography changes between controls.

Desktop alignment is orderly but visually static, and mobile becomes a long sequence of oversized stacked rectangles. Large internal padding and irregular inter-section gaps create bulk without meaningful changes in pace.

The page offers no product photography, illustration, packaging, bread texture or other material that lets visitors assess the bakery's core product. Type and flat beige panels are not developed strongly enough to compensate.

Captured controls are visibly inconsistent: one Add action resembles a tiny default button, another is an underlined text link and another is a large pill. Hover, focus, feedback and transition states were not provided and cannot be assessed.

The mobile view remains readable and avoids overflow, but it is essentially the desktop layout stacked into one column. There is no visible reprioritization, regrouping or mobile-specific density strategy.

Cream and brown tones are plausible for an artisan bakery, and the plainspoken presentation suits a small local shop. The treatment remains too generic and inconsistently crafted to feel recognizably Fold & Grain.

The opening sentence immediately explains the business, product availability is concise, ordering is repeatedly signposted and collection timing and location are explicit. The screenshots do not show prices, quantities, availability states or the actual ordering flow.

It avoids most familiar generated-site clichés such as gradient headlines, fake metrics, icon triplets and glowing decoration. However, the generic card stack and lightly branded minimalism still feel assembled rather than meaningfully derived from the bakery.
No image, composition, typographic gesture or visible interaction creates a signature moment. The bakery name and bread descriptions are more memorable than the design.

verdicts.rationale: The page communicates the bakery, products, collection terms and location clearly, but the visual execution is below professional standard. Inconsistent card treatments, mismatched button styles, weak product representation and a mobile layout that merely stacks the desktop components make it feel like unfinished styling rather than a resolved brand experience.

criterionScores.note: The restrained palette is coherent, but plain typography, rules, fields and green buttons do not establish a distinctive visual thesis.
Specificity resides almost entirely in the headline and supporting copy. The structure and visual treatment could serve many unrelated professional-service businesses.

The proposition, enquiry form and pricing link are easy to find, but the visible homepage omits service detail, process, proof, credentials and reassurance. Pricing is oddly reduced to a link after appearing in the navigation.

The hero headline leads clearly, followed by the main CTA and enquiry form. Lower sections are easy to scan, though the large gap beside the desktop form weakens balance and the sequence has little modulation.

Rules and generous spacing create basic rhythm, but each section follows the same left-aligned pattern. The desktop form button sits awkwardly beside the textarea, while much of the right column remains unused.
Using type and space alone can suit an accountancy practice, but here those materials are too thinly developed to explain expertise, demonstrate process or build trust.

Buttons, links and form controls appear clear and consistently styled in the static images. Hover, focus, validation, submission feedback and navigation behavior were not captured, so deeper interaction craft cannot be judged.

The mobile layout remains legible and correctly stacks the form controls, but it is essentially a narrower version of the desktop page. Navigation stays crowded in one row, and the hero wrapping is not carefully composed for the phone.
The sober typography, white space and muted green are plausible for a dependable bookkeeping service. They communicate generic seriousness rather than a recognisable Sable & Finch character.

The audience, service category, turnover range and primary next step are stated immediately. Conversion confidence is limited by the absence of visible proof, service scope, credentials, pricing context or an explanation of what happens after enquiry.

The page avoids many conspicuous generated-design clichés such as gradients, card grids, fake metrics and glowing decoration. Nevertheless, its generic minimal-service-site structure and undifferentiated empty space feel default rather than business-derived.

verdicts.rationale: The page is functional, legible and commercially direct, but it looks like a minimally styled template rather than an authored identity for a specialist bookkeeping firm. The sparse homepage provides little evidence, differentiation or trust-building content, and the mobile version is essentially the same composition stacked into one column.

The optometry connection exists almost entirely in the copy. The structure and styling could be reused for many local appointment businesses with minimal changes.

Service summary, booking form, and contact details appear in a sensible basic order, but the page lacks visible navigation, service detail, credentials, opening hours, pricing guidance, or trust information.

Project names and studio copy provide some specificity, but the structure and styling could be transferred almost unchanged to another design, architecture or strategy studio.

The hero dominates immediately and section titles, project names and metadata form a clear reading order. Later sections are comparatively uniform and subdued, so the page loses emphasis after the opening.

Large spatial pauses create a calm editorial rhythm, but several gaps feel excessive rather than purposeful, particularly on desktop, while the repeated ruled rows and sparse lower sections flatten the scroll.

Static screenshots show orderly navigation and likely link targets, but provide no evidence of hover, focus, transition, feedback or other interaction states. Those aspects cannot be credited from the supplied evidence.

Mobile adapts type scale, stacks the approach columns and converts project metadata into vertical blocks cleanly. It is still fundamentally the desktop sequence narrowed into one column, with the service ticker clipped and desktop navigation apparently removed without a visible replacement.

The screenshots show straightforward navigation and contact links, but no hover, focus, transition, feedback or other interaction states are visible, so higher craft cannot be evidenced.

criterionScores.note: The restrained serif-led presentation is coherent and suitable, but it amounts to a familiar professional-services aesthetic rather than a strong visual thesis.
